entities.summary: A short volcanic-rock hike with towers, walls and steep natural steps that feels disproportionately mountainous for a 539 m hill close to Prague.
entities.description: Bořeň is a freestanding volcanic hill above Bílina with an unusually rocky character for its modest elevation. The recommended loop uses the legal hiking approach to the summit and passes rough stone, steep natural steps and extensive rock walls rather than treating the hill as a roadside viewpoint. Dry conditions are strongly preferable; ice or wet rock changes the difficulty significantly.
entities.whyWorthwhile: A high geological payoff for a short outing and roughly D1 travel from Prague. Milešovka is the larger panoramic landmark, while Bořeň delivers much more direct rock terrain per kilometre.

entities.summary: A White Carpathian meadow loop that becomes a national-level destination during the late-spring orchid and flower peak, when species-rich grassland and solitary trees align.
entities.description: The route from Lučina follows the Orchidejová nature-trail circuit through the Čertoryje landscape and related meadow sites. The reserve is exceptionally species-rich, but its catalogue value is strongly seasonal: outside the flowering period it is a very good meadow landscape; during the right late-spring window the visual and ecological experience can jump to S-tier quality. Visitors must stay on designated paths in the reserve and should not approach individual flowers off trail.
entities.whyWorthwhile: This is the clearest seasonal transformation in the Czech research. Ordinary quality is around A/D2; a strong late-May to mid-June flowering peak can justify D4 and a dedicated cross-country trip.

entities.summary: A compact but rugged Vltava cliff traverse whose chains, rocky forest trail and six viewpoints deliver substantially more hiking intensity than its short distance suggests.
entities.description: This loop follows the protected Drbákov–Albertovy skály trail above the Vltava/Slapy landscape. It combines steep forest slopes, exposed-looking but non-technical rocky passages, roots, steps, chains and a sequence of viewpoints rather than reducing the outing to one overlook. Visitors should remain on the official route inside the reserve, and wet leaves or rock make the trail materially harder.
entities.whyWorthwhile: One of the strongest Prague-return anomalies in the research: roughly D1 travel friction for a D2-quality hiking experience. It is more intimate and physically engaging than many better-known Vltava viewpoints while still fitting into a half-day.

entities.summary: A Český les borderland walk where a substantial vanished village remains physically legible through exposed foundations, cemetery traces and the surrounding depopulated landscape.
entities.description: This loop from Mýtnice approaches the former village of Grafenried/Lučina through the Czech-German border landscape. Unlike many historical-map curiosities, enough building foundations, cemetery and settlement structure survive or have been exposed that the erased village can be understood on the ground. The hike is modest by itself; its strongest use is as part of a broader Český les historical-landscape weekend.
entities.whyWorthwhile: The historical-map anomaly survives the real visitor-quality test: the absence of the old settlement is physically legible rather than merely archival. It earns A quality for historical landscape, though the actual Prague drive is slightly greater than the D2 experience justifies as a standalone trip.

entities.summary: A 24 km Český ráj circuit that turns familiar sandstone geology into a serious hiking day by linking Klokočské průchody, Kozákov and Rotštejn.
entities.description: This official long route starts and ends at Turnov station and links Klokočské průchody, sandstone formations, Kozákov, Rotštejn and quieter connective terrain. Its value is the complete walking experience rather than any single attraction. It avoids the usual short headline-rock circuit and gives enough distance and ascent to feel like a full hiking day while remaining public-transport friendly.
entities.whyWorthwhile: Český ráj is famous, but this route is a less conventional way to experience it and is much more substantial than the standard postcard loops. It earns D2 because the route itself remains rewarding across its connectors, not only at the famous nodes.

entities.summary: A wild-feeling loop from Mimoň that shifts from sandstone formations to basalt summit terrain and castle ruins inside the former Ralsko military landscape.
entities.description: The route starts at Mimoň railway station, passes Vranov and the publicly accessible Juliina vyhlídka, climbs through increasingly rugged terrain to the Ralsko summit ruins, then returns through forest. The appeal is the transition between sandstone, basalt boulder and wall terrain, woodland and the former-military cultural landscape. The route does not require scrambling onto protected sandstone towers.
entities.whyWorthwhile: The combination of geology, ruins, forest and former military landscape feels much stranger and wilder than its roughly D1 travel time from Prague suggests. Bezděz has the more intact castle; this route has the more unusual landscape journey.

entities.summary: A quieter eastern-Krkonoše traverse through old beech woodland, mountain meadows, wetlands, mining traces and the vanished settlement landscape of Sklenářovice.
entities.description: The official point-to-point route runs from Svoboda nad Úpou across the Rýchory and Dvorský les area, then through the Sklenářovice landscape to Mladé Buky. It combines old woodland, meadow and wetland scenery with traces of mining and a vanished mountain settlement, so the historical layer improves an already strong landscape hike rather than serving as isolated archaeology.
entities.whyWorthwhile: Normally an A/D2 route, but peak beech colour combined with mist or low cloud can make the forest atmosphere worth a cross-country trip. It is much quieter and more enclosed than the iconic central-Krkonoše ridge experience.

entities.summary: A proper river-gorge hike with boulders, rapids, cascades and rough riverside trail, paired with a higher return route instead of a simple waterfall out-and-back.
entities.description: The loop runs from Chotěboř through the Doubrava gorge toward Bílek and returns on higher terrain. Several kilometres closely follow the river through boulder-filled and eroded gorge scenery with occasional chains or protected passages. Normal post-rain flow improves the atmosphere, but heavy rain can put sections of the riverside path under water and winter ice materially increases difficulty.
entities.whyWorthwhile: The gorge offers substantially more hiking substance than many Czech waterfall outings and earns its longer Prague journey. The walking itself remains the attraction rather than merely transportation to one photogenic cascade.

entities.summary: A tiny volcanic hill whose fissure-ventilation phenomenon turns an otherwise modest walk into a disproportionately interesting winter geological excursion during hard frost.
entities.description: The Boreč nature trail is short and easy in ordinary conditions, but the destination changes character in sustained winter cold. Warm, humid air moving through the fractured volcanic hill can emerge from summit fissures and become conspicuous against freezing ambient air. The phenomenon is condition-driven rather than date-driven; snow and ice can also make the little trail substantially slipperier.
entities.whyWorthwhile: Normally only a B/D0.5–D1 outing, but during a properly cold spell the unusual ventarole phenomenon can justify D2 travel from Prague. It is a compact geological experience rather than a summit-view hike.

entities.summary: A dense small-town and river-valley loop combining Rabštejn’s historic fabric with ruins, Střela scenery, old slate workings, mills and fortification traces.
entities.description: The marked Rabštejn nature trail links the tiny historic settlement with the Střela valley, castle and fortification remnants, old slate quarrying, mills and viewpoints. Its strength is density and layering rather than one spectacular natural feature. From Prague it is a good historical-landscape outing, but not as strong a pure travel-return anomaly as Drbákov, Ralsko or Bořeň.
entities.whyWorthwhile: A very good layered cultural-landscape walk and useful catalogue entry, but deliberately retained at B/D1: the actual drive is longer than the experience’s general-purpose draw, unless the visitor is particularly interested in historical landscape and settlement history.
